subject.title: feat(dashboard): sandboxed custom widgets + approval flow [3/3]

question: Should OpenClaw accept an enabled-by-default bundled dashboard custom-widget security surface after redesigning widget asset auth, content-bound approval, and SQLite state storage, or should this stack remain experimental/out of core for now?
rationale: The PR adds agent-authored browser code, unauthenticated serving, persisted operator state, and dependency graph changes; choosing the acceptable trust model and storage contract is a maintainer/security decision rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Pause and redesign before merge
options.body: Require authenticated or capability-scoped asset loading, approval tied to a validated content digest/version, SQLite/plugin-state persistence, and dependency/security approval before another merge review.

options.title: Accept as experimental core surface
options.body: Maintainers could intentionally accept the unauthenticated static route, mutable approval semantics, and JSON state as temporary debt, but that should be an explicit documented security/product exception.

options.title: Move custom widgets out of core
options.body: Keep the dashboard workspace work separate and route agent-authored custom widgets to a plugin/ClawHub experiment until the core security boundary is proven.

recommendation.title: Pause and redesign before merge
recommendation.body: Require authenticated or capability-scoped asset loading, approval tied to a validated content digest/version, SQLite/plugin-state persistence, and dependency/security approval before another merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-main owner signal for the plugin-state and bundled Control UI tab surfaces implicated by the decision.
